turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Howzit. Come through, I'll get your vitals before the doctor calls you. On the scale, please.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, alright. I've been nervous the whole drive. Is he very behind today?

[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): A bit, ja. The computer's been sulking all morning. Seventy-eight point four kilograms. Blood pressure one twenty-eight over eighty-four, pulse fifty-eight, temperature thirty-six point two.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Seventy-eight? Shame, I was near seventy-two before winter. Is a pulse of fifty-eight too slow, should I worry?
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): That's the doctor's call, hey. Have a seat, he'll be in just now.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this screen's frozen again. Right. What's been going on?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm exhausted, and I'm cold all the time. I keep a jersey on at work when everyone else wants the aircon off.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again? Wrong tab. Tired, and cold?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. Proper tired, and cold even on the couch at home. Since about April, so four months, unless it started in March, I really can't pin it. I'm fifty-one, accounts manager at a logistics place, desk till late, and I put it down to the job.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Long hours will do that. I don't think we need bloods. We'll call it burnout and I'll see you in a month.

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): A month and no tests? There's more, though. The weight's up about six kilos over those months. I'm constipated, that's new, I go every few days, and my mood's flat, not crying, just not myself, and I keep blaming my age.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hang on, I was still on the burnout note. Weight, bowels, low mood. Any thoughts of hurting yourself?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. I still pitch up at work. My husband says I fuss too much, he swallows his metformin and gets on with the day, diabetes, his, not mine.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): His metformin, understood. Hair coming out? Palpitations? Any chest pain?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Hair's the same. No palpitations, no chest pain. Skin's a bit dry, I don't know if that counts.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Dry skin, noted. Do you take any regular medicine yourself?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. My sister takes biotin, the strong capsules, for her hair, and she keeps on at me to start. I haven't had a single one. A Panado now and then if my head's sore.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Allergies, to tablets or anything?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none that I know of.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Family side, thyroid problems? The cursor jumped, say it once more, slowly.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): My mum has an underactive thyroid, Eltroxin for years. She reckons I sound like she did. Is it hereditary? If it is, am I on tablets for the rest of my life?
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): It can run in families, that doesn't mean lifelong tablets. Have you had a thyroid blood test before? I'm opening the old labs, the system's crawling.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): About two years back. Borderline, they said. I can hear them saying borderline.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Up at last. TSH was one point eight. Normal, not borderline, so that memory doesn't match the result.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Normal? Are you sure it's my file and not someone else's? I was so sure. Am I wasting your time with this?
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): It's your file, don't stress. With the weight, the constipation and your mum, I'm changing the plan. We won't sit on it for a month, we'll do the bloods.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh good, because I was going to argue. If the TSH is high, do you start me on Eltroxin the same day? I really don't want tablets unless I need them. How long do results take?

[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): No tablets from me today. If it's clearly underactive we talk treatment when the number's in, usually two or three working days. This could be an underactive thyroid, or it could just be the hours and turning fifty. Bloods are how we tell.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): What about the constipation, do I buy something at the chemist? And can I keep these work hours? I'm scared it's cancer. Sorry, I know I ask a lot.

[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nothing you've told me sounds like cancer. Stay at work, but cut the late nights if you can manage. More water, a bit of fruit, a short walk. If you're very stuck, get lactulose from the chemist, but try the simple things first.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): I used to walk the dog every evening, I've dropped it, I'm too tired. My sister says biotin messes with thyroid bloods, hers not mine, I promise I'm not taking it. Is six kilos a dangerous amount? I also lie awake worrying some nights, not every night.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Not on biotin, so that's not a problem for the test. Six kilos isn't dangerous by itself. Sorry, give me the weight again, this window just refreshed.

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): About six kilos up. Your nurse got seventy-eight point four today, and before winter I was near seventy-two. There's a lovely jacaranda outside, I got distracted looking at it, sorry.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll stick with her seventy-eight point four. Jacarandas can wait. Any chance of pregnancy? Should have asked that sooner.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No, definitely not. I had a hysterectomy eight years ago, fibroids. No periods since.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ok. Hands are cool. Pulse is regular, fifty-eight, same as the nurse. Thyroid gland feels normal, no swelling in the neck, and the tummy's soft.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): If the gland is normal, what's the point of a blood test? And my mood, the lying awake, do I need a counsellor?
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Say that again? I was typing the request and I missed half.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Gland feels normal, so why test me? Should I see someone for the mood?

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Feeling normal doesn't clear it. I'm ordering TSH and free T4, and a full blood count, today. If the tests are normal and you're still flat, then we look at counselling. Not a referral today.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. Can your nurse take the blood before I leave? When do I come back, and what if I slide downhill before then?
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back next week and we'll go through the results, whatever they show.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Next week. And if I can't get out of bed, or my stomach's really sore?
[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): If you feel much worse, or you get severe belly pain, come back sooner or go to the emergency unit. Otherwise next week still stands.
[SEG0045] person_1 (NURSE): I can bleed you now. TSH, free T4, full blood count. Which arm?
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Left one's fine. Will I bruise? I bruised a bit last time at the chemist, maybe I was just tense.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): A bit of bruising happens. Press on the cotton wool afterwards. You're not on anything that thins the blood.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. Press, left arm, next week. Thank you, I feel a bit better just having a plan.

spec.situation: Middle-aged person tired and cold for months, weight up, constipated, low mood; pins it on work and age; mother had thyroid disease; one old thyroid test result recalled wrongly ('borderline, they said'). Blood test planned.
features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: TSH is discussed as prior result and newly ordered, but completion status today isn't stated.
Advice is from doctor, not responsible person patient.
bad.text: Do not start thyroid tablets today; discuss treatment only if the result shows clear underactivity (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: Patient reported previous thyroid blood test about 2 years ago; doctor reviewed old labs and stated prior TSH was 1.8 and normal, not borderline as the patient remembered.
Patient denied taking any regular medicine.
Patient specifically said she has not taken any biotin despite her sister encouraging it; doctor noted biotin is not a problem for the thyroid test because she is not taking it.
Low mood detail missing: patient said she was 'not crying, just not myself.'
Patient said she still pitches up at work despite symptoms.
Patient expressed worry that it might be cancer.
Patient reported bruising a bit last time after blood was taken at the chemist.
Doctor initially said he did not think blood tests were needed, would call it burnout and review in a month, then changed plan after hearing about weight gain, constipation and family history.
Doctor advised results usually take two or three working days.
Doctor said if tests are normal and she is still flat, counselling would be considered, but not a referral today.
Doctor said follow-up next week would be to go through the results, whatever they show.
Planned blood draw before leaving was confirmed by nurse: TSH, free T4, and full blood count to be taken immediately.
